importance_ranking.reason: Prefabricated buildings span visually distinct sub-types — PEB industrial sheds, LGSF residential homes, modular panel buildings, cold storage structures — that buyers cannot distinguish from title or specs alone. A buyer scanning listings for a warehouse shed will immediately skip a listing showing a residential modular home; image is the fastest sub-type filter available.

Built type, material (PEB/LGSF/panel), clear span, and frame type are primary shortlisting criteria — a factory owner needs a clear-span PEB, not a multi-span residential frame. Without these specs visible on the listing, buyers cannot determine fit and will not engage.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Recognised PEB brands — Interarch, EPACK Prefab, Kirby Building Systems, Pennar Industries, Everest Industries — carry significant buyer trust signals; institutional and large industrial buyers actively specify or prefer named manufacturers with ISO 9001 certification and proven erection track records.
importance_ranking.reason: For large capital projects (warehouses, factories, government buildings), buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials, ISO certification, seismic zone design capability, and post-erection service network during vendor shortlisting — company identity is a qualification gate, not just a preference.

Per-sq-ft rates vary substantially with material type (PEB vs LGSF vs panel), clear span, insulation, and number of floors — buyers cannot compare prices across listings without confirmed spec equivalence. Indian B2B buyers are price-aggressive but price comparison is only meaningful after sub-type and spec alignment.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Large turnkey/EPC contracts are quoted as lump-sum project values; steel frame-only supply is sometimes quoted per MT by fabricators. Per sq ft is the dominant and expected unit for supply-and-erect contracts across industrial, commercial, and residential prefab segments.
importance_ranking.reason: Unit is non-obvious in this category — sellers quote per sq ft, per MT (steel frame only), or per project (lump sum turnkey), and a buyer comparing per-sq-ft listings against a per-project quote cannot make a valid price comparison without the unit being explicitly shown.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Material (PEB Steel / LGSF / Insulated Panel / MS Structure / Container Based) defines the structural system and is non-interchangeable — a buyer requiring a PEB steel warehouse cannot substitute an insulated panel building, and each material type carries a fundamentally different price point and engineering requirement.

Frame type (Clear Span / Multi-Span / Multi-Gable / Single Slope / Lean-To) drives the largest price delta within the PEB segment — clear-span structures require heavier primary frames and cost significantly more per sq ft than multi-span equivalents, and buyers with specific operational requirements (crane bays, unobstructed floor area) cannot substitute one frame type for another.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Eave height is a primary PEB configurator — industrial buyers specify minimum clear height for crane operation, racking systems, or aircraft hangars, and height directly drives column size, steel tonnage, and per-sq-ft cost.

Steel grade (IS 2062 E250 / E350 / E450) determines structural capacity and compliance with NBC 2016 seismic zone requirements — buyers in high-seismic zones or with heavy crane loads specify minimum steel grade, and it is a significant cost and compliance differentiator.

Roofing sheet profile and coating (Galvalume / colour-coated / bare Galvanised) affects weatherproofing, thermal performance, and aesthetics — buyers for cold storage, food processing, and commercial buildings specify roofing type as a compliance and durability requirement.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Total built-up area is the primary project-scoping signal — it determines steel tonnage, erection timeline, and total project cost, allowing sellers to immediately assess whether the project is within their capacity and quote accurately.

Wall material (PUF Panel / EPS Panel / Steel / Cement Panel / Glass Wool Panel) defines the structural and thermal system of the building — sellers need this to determine which product line applies, confirm compliance with the buyer's use case (e.g., cold storage requires PUF), and price the project.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know whether the buyer wants a factory shed, warehouse, residential home, cold storage, or office building — the structural design, compliance requirements, and product line differ fundamentally across use cases and this is the single most important routing signal for a seller.
